Headings.text: Headings help provide a hierarchy for the screen's content, and allow people using a screen reader to quickly jump between sections. Numbered headings (H1,H2 etc)  are not supported by iOS or Android.

Focus grouping.text:
Grouping elements like the contents of a tile or cell can make for a better experience when using assistive technology.

If multiple actions are in the group more instruction will be needed on how this will behave.

Reading order.text:
Designing the order that keyboard-only or screen reader users will flow through the content can improve their experience.

Typically, focus order (the order of interactive elements, e.g moving with the TAB key) aligns with reading order (the order of all content e.g. using the down arrow key, or 'say all' command with a screen reader).

Alt text.text:
Alternative text is announced by screen readers and describes the purpose, function, or content of an image.

Images that convey meaning are informative and require alt text. Images that do not convey meaning, or are non-functional and beside text that conveys their meaning are considered decorative.

Contrast.text: Text must have a contrast ratio of 4.5:1. Large text must have a contrast ratio of 3:1. Interactive and meaningful graphical elements must have a contrast ratio of 3:1.

Touch target.text:
WCAG SC 2.5.8 Target Size defines the minimum area as 24px by 24px. Some teams prefer to use 44px x 44px for iOS and 48px x 48px for Android.

There are exceptions for undersize targets with sufficient spacing, links within sentences or blocks of text, or targets like pins on a map, or dots on a chart.

Use this step of Include as a tool to check where needed; it may not be necessary to annotate every target in every design.

Text zoom.text: Mobile devices allow users to customize text sizes. Ensure the layout will adapt to respect these user preferences.

Complex gestures.text: When actions can be performed with a gesture ensure there is an alternate and visible way to perform this using one finger and taps.

Color blindness.text: People may perceive colors differently, and may not be able to differentiate between some or all colors. Ensure a design does not rely only on color to convey meaning.

Landmarks.text:
Landmarks identify regions of a screen and help people who use assistive technology to make a mental model of a screen's content.

When creating multiple landmarks of the same type you'll be prompted to a short label. Do not include words like 'landmark', 'region' or 'navigation' in the label as screen readers already announce the type.

Typically, focus order (the order of interactive elements, e.g moving with the TAB key) aligns with reading order (the order of all content e.g. using the down arrow key, or 'say all' command with a screen reader).

Alternative text is announced by screen readers and describes the purpose, function, or content of an image.

Images that convey meaning are informative and require alt text. Images that do not convey meaning, or are non-functional and beside text that conveys their meaning are considered decorative.

Contrast.text:
Text must have a contrast ratio of 4.5:1. Large text must have a contrast ratio of 3:1. Interactive and meaningful graphical elements must have a contrast ratio of 3:1.

Large text is 24px or greater, or 19px bold or greater. In CSS, bold text typically has font-weight:bold, or font-weight:700 or greater.

Touch target.text:
WCAG SC 2.5.8 Target Size defines the minimum area as 24px by 24px, but allows exceptions for undersize targets with sufficient spacing, links within sentences or blocks of text, or targets like pins on a map, or dots on a chart.

Use this step of Include as a tool to check where needed; it may not be necessary to annotate every target in every design.

Text zoom.text:
Users must be able to resize text at least 200% without loss of information. Enlarge the text in your design and consider how the content and layout is impacted.

This step aligns with WCAG SC 1.4.4 Resize text

Responsive reflow.text:
Web content needs to reflow, without horizontal scrolling, at a screen width of 320px, Text does not need to resize to meet this, but if it does, no information must be lost.

This step aligns with WCAG SC 1.4.10 Reflow.

Interactive elements.text: Naming interactive elements determines what the screen reader is going to read out. Accessibility for each interactive element from the storybook is already coded in the control.

Focus grouping.text: Grouping can improve usability of accessibility services, e.g. it reduces the number of swipes to move through content with a screen reader. If a group contains multiple actions, align with design on the preferred approach, such as 'custom actions'.

Reading order.text:
When using a mobile screen reader, the reading order and focus order typically align, including when using an external keyboard. Check TalkBack and VoiceOver support for correct key combinations.

Focus order annotations are useful for showing how the app supports a keyboard without a screen reader running. Android enables this support without a system setting change. For iOS, enable Full Keyboard Access in Accessibility settings.

Alt text.text:
Alternative text is announced by screen readers and describes the purpose, function, or content of an image.

Images that convey meaning are informative and require alt text. Images that do not convey meaning, or are non-functional and beside text that conveys their meaning are considered decorative.

Contrast.text: Text must have a contrast ratio of 4.5:1. Large text must have a contrast ratio of 3:1. Interactive and meaningful graphical elements must have a contrast ratio of 3:1.

Touch target.text:
WCAG SC 2.5.8 Target Size defines the minimum area as 24px by 24px. Some teams prefer to use 44px x 44px for iOS and 48px x 48px for Android.

There are exceptions for undersize targets with sufficient spacing, links within sentences or blocks of text, or targets like pins on a map, or dots on a chart.

Text zoom.text:
Apps need to support enlarged text sizes up to 200% which users can set in Android or iOS display or accessibility settings. In practice, it is common to cap or limit resizing of some elements. Discuss with design where needed.

This step aligns with WCAG SC 1.4.4.

Complex gestures.text: When actions can be performed with a gesture, ensure there is at least one alternate way to perform this using one finger and taps. As this requirement supports sighted users with limited dexterity but who may not be using assistive technology, the alternate method must be visible. Custom actions can also support assistive technology users.

Color blindness.text: People may perceive colors differently, and may not be able to differentiate between some or all colors. Ensure a design does not rely only on color to convey meaning.

Landmarks.text:
HTML5 elements such as <main>, <nav>, <footer> identify landmarks - regions of a page which help screen reader users navigate and understand layout.

When there are multiple landmarks of the same type they should be named using aria-label. Names must not include words like 'landmark', 'region' or 'navigation' as screen readers already announce the type.

Headings.text: Headings provide a hierarchy for the screen's content, and allow people using a screen reader to quickly jump between sections. Use only one H1 per page, avoid skipping heading levels, and make them succinct.

Reading order.text:
Reading order refers to all content in the DOM. It's the order a screen reader announces content when using "read all" or line-by-line commands.

Focus order applies only to interactive elements, and follows the order in which they receive keyboard focus (e.g., using Tab or arrow keys).

These orders usually align. Focus order annotations indicate order between and within interactive elements, and can indicate where the focus order diverges from reading order.

Always test both—regardless of whether annotations are provided.

Alt text.text:
Alternative text is announced by screen readers and describes the purpose, function, or content of an image.

Images that convey meaning are informative and require alt text. Images that do not convey meaning, or are non-functional and beside text that conveys their meaning are considered decorative.

Contrast.text:
Text must have a contrast ratio of 4.5:1. Large text must have a contrast ratio of 3:1. Interactive and meaningful graphical elements must have a contrast ratio of 3:1.

Contrast minimums apply to hover and visited states, but interactive elements in a disabled state are exempt.

Touch target.text: WCAG SC 2.5.8 Target Size defines the minimum area as 24px by 24px, but allows exceptions for undersize targets with sufficient spacing, links within sentences or blocks of text, or targets like pins on a map, or dots on a chart.

Text zoom.text:
Users must be able to resize text at least 200% without loss of information. This applies to all breakpoints.

Users can change text size in browser settings. This change makes text larger but will not affect some non-text elements. Alternatively, users can zoom the browser to 200% which will resize other elements.

Common failures for this requirement include text becoming clipped, overlapping, or extending beyond containers to the point where meaning is lost.

This step aligns with WCAG SC 1.4.4.

Responsive reflow.text: Web content needs to reflow, without horizontal scrolling, at a screen width of 320px. Text does not need to resize to meet this, but if it does, no information must be lost. This step aligns with WCAG SC 1.4.10 Reflow.
